ELI5: What causes an airplane to drop and go into those brief moments of free fall?

Turbulence, the plane runs into a patch of air that's blowing downwards or the same direction as it, so the plane loses lift. There's also the ground effect where when a plane is close to the ground, the air pushed down by the wings gets compressed between the wings and the ground, meaning a plane gets vastly more lift at low altitudes, then when they start to move above the altitude where ground effect still happens they lose that extra lift and need to move faster to get the same lift, so the plane drops a bit. https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ground_effect_(aerodynamics)
